questions.stem: A maximization model's LP relaxation, solved correctly, has value 812.4. A colleague reports a yes/no plan that obeys every row and is worth 830. What can you conclude?

options.text: The plan is fine, since an LP value is a floor that plans can always pass
options.says: For a maximization the relaxation's value is an upper bound: every allowed plan is a point of the LP.

options.text: The best plan is worth 830, since any plan found tops the LP value
options.says: No allowed plan can sit above the LP value, so finding one means the plan or its check is wrong.

options.text: The report is wrong, since 812.4 is a ceiling that no allowed plan passes
options.says: Right: every allowed 0-1 plan is a point of the relaxation, so its value is at most the LP's 812.4.

options.text: The LP needs a tighter tolerance, since its value should match 830
options.says: The LP was solved correctly; a tolerance changes values by tiny amounts, never by 17.6.

origin.section: Dropping Integrality Gives an LP Whose Value Bounds Every Plan From Above

questions.stem: A node allows 1 to 8 crews, and the node's LP sets the crew count to 3.4. Which two children does branching on the crew count make?

options.text: Crews from 1 to 3, and crews from 4 to 8
options.says: Right: down is crews <= floor(3.4) = 3 and up is crews >= ceil(3.4) = 4, each keeping the other end of 1..8.

options.text: Crews fixed at 3, and crews fixed at 4
options.says: Fixing loses every plan with 1, 2 or 5 to 8 crews; branching only caps or raises one end of the range.

options.text: Crews from 1 to 3.4, and crews from 3.4 to 8
options.says: Both children would still allow 3.4, so the fractional LP point would come back.

options.text: Crews fixed at 0, and crews fixed at 1
options.says: 0 and 1 are the floor and ceiling of a value between 0 and 1; for 3.4 they are 3 and 4.

origin.section: A General Integer Branches on Floor and Ceiling

questions.stem: Deep in a tree, a node's LP solution sets every 0-1 variable to exactly 0 or 1, with value 950. Its parent's LP value was 990. What does the search do at this node?

options.text: Branch on the variable at 1 with the largest value, to look for a better plan
options.says: Nothing in the node beats its LP value, and this plan reaches it; splitting further can never find more.

options.text: Drop the node unread, since its value fell below its parent's
options.says: A child's value is never above its parent's; falling below is normal and says nothing against the plan.

options.text: Re-solve the parent with this plan fixed, to confirm the value 950
options.says: The node's LP already holds this plan's rows and fixings; its solution is a real plan as it stands.

options.text: Stop there, keeping the plan worth 950 as the best one inside that node
options.says: Right: an integral LP solution is the best plan in its node, so the node is a leaf.

origin.section: Branching Stops at a Node Whose LP Is Infeasible or Integral
